diagnostic_evidence.quote: for a scalar $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}$ is known as $\epsilon$-pseudoeigenfunction and is physically relevant since

issues.failure_explanation: Telescoping gives ‖K_F^n g − λ^n g‖ ≤ ε Σ_{j<n}‖K_F‖^j|λ|^{n−1−j} ≤ nε·max(‖K_F‖,|λ|)^{n−1}, which is O(nε) for all n only if max(‖K_F‖,|λ|) ≤ 1; no such hypothesis is imposed (λ is an arbitrary complex scalar, and F need not be measure-preserving, so ‖K_F‖ may exceed 1). Counterexample: for any measure-preserving F, take g the normalized constant, λ = 2, ε = 1: ‖(K_F−2I)g‖ = 1 ≤ ε, yet ‖K_F^n g − 2^n g‖ = 2^n − 1, not O(nε). The same false claim is repeated unlabelled in the Appendix.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypotheses ‖K_F‖ ≤ 1 and |λ| ≤ 1 (automatic for measure-preserving systems with spectral λ), or state the correct bound O(nε·max(‖K_F‖,|λ|)^{n−1}).
issues.overall_effect: The motivational claim about the physical relevance of pseudoeigenfunctions (stated twice) is unreliable for |λ| > 1 or ‖K_F‖ > 1; no theorem or algorithm relies on it.
issues.title: False O(nε) propagation bound for ε-pseudoeigenfunctions
issues.why_classification: A local correction of a standalone displayed motivational claim; all theorems, algorithms and guarantees are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $\Omega_{\mathcal{X}}^m\subset\Omega_{\mathcal{X}}$, we need only prove the classification for the problem function $\Xi_{\spec_{\mathrm{ap}}}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Ω^m_X is defined (main text and appendix) as the measure-preserving maps with no continuity requirement, while Ω_X additionally requires continuity; measure-preserving does not imply continuity, so the proof's premise 'Ω^m_X ⊂ Ω_X' is false. Hence the claimed two-limit convergence for all F ∈ Ω^m is false: for 𝒳 = S¹, Ω^m contains thm:rotation(c)'s class of possibly discontinuous m.p. invertible maps, for which the paper itself proves that computing the spectrum (equal to spec_ap, since K_F is unitary) is impossible for a tower of general algorithms of any height (SCI = ∞). Thus thm2's 'Two limits for Ω^m' bullet and thm:general_koopman_computation's Σ_2^G classification for Ω^m are false as stated and contradict thm:rotation(c) internally.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require continuity in Ω^m_X (i.e., Ω^m := Ω^m ∩ Ω_X) in both the main-text and appendix definitions; then Ω^m ⊂ Ω_X holds (m.p. ⇒ non-singular, K_F an isometry) and the existing proof applies verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: thm2's Ω^m guarantee, the appendix's Ω^m classifications, the placement of Ω^m in the SCI-hierarchy figure, and the appendix summary 'the SCI of computing the spectrum of measure-preserving systems is ≤ 2' are unreliable for the class as defined.
issues.title: Class Ω^m_X omits continuity, making the two-limit computability claims false and contradicting thm:rotation(c)
issues.why_classification: A headline theorem is false for its stated class (the truth is the opposite, SCI = ∞) and contradicts another theorem of the paper, which is more than a degenerate-case fix; but the forced repair is a single local hypothesis that preserves every intended result, so it is not serious.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose says the penultimate limit in (Sigma_example) (the Ω^α case) is contained in the spectrum (Σ behaviour) and that in (Pi_example) (the Ω^m case) covers it (Π behaviour). The equations state the opposite: (Sigma_example) says spec_ap ⊂ limit + B, i.e. the limit covers the spectrum (Π-type), and (Pi_example) says limit ⊂ spec_ap + B (Σ-type), matching the appendix's Π_2^G for Ω^α and Σ_2^G for Ω^m. The prose (and the label names Sigma_example/Pi_example) invert the verification types of the two parts of thm2.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If such a $k$ exists with $h_{n_2,k}(z,F)\in I_{n_2}^1(\epsilon)$, then $z\in \Gamma_{n_2,n_1}(F)$. Otherwise, $z\notin \Gamma_{n_2,n_1}(F)$.

Since the sequence $h_{n_2,j}(z,F)$ cannot visit both intervals $I_{n_2}^1(\epsilon)$ and $I_{n_2}^2(\epsilon)$ infinitely often as $n_1\rightarrow\infty$, it follows that the limit $\lim_{n_1\rightarrow\infty}\Gamma_{n_2,n_1}(F)=\Gamma_{n_2}(F)$ exists.

issues.failure_explanation: With h_{n_2,j} → h_{n_2} and Γ_{n_2} defined by the last visit to I_1 ∪ I_2: (i) if h_{n_2}(z) ∈ [ε−1/n_2, ε−1/(2n_2)), the sequence may converge inside the gap after an early I_2 visit, so z ∉ Γ_{n_2} although h_{n_2}(z) < ε−1/(2n_2) — the left inclusion fails; (ii) if the last I_1 visit is followed by gap-convergence to a limit in (ε, ε+1/(2n_2)], then z ∈ Γ_{n_2} with h_{n_2}(z) > ε — the right inclusion, and hence the claimed guarantee Γ_{n_2} ⊂ spec_{ap,ε}, fails by up to 1/(2n_2). The rule is also indexed by 'j = 1,…,n_2' where the inner limit index n_1 is intended. The correct sandwich is {h < ε−1/n_2} ⊂ Γ_{n_2} ⊂ {h ≤ ε+1/(2n_2)}, which yields the Σ_2^G classification only after tightening the interval widths (e.g. to 2^{-n_2}).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-derive the sandwich with tightened, exponentially calibrated interval widths (e.g. I_1 = [0, ε−2^{-n_2}], I_2 = [ε+2^{-n_2−1}, ∞)) and correct the summation index; the construction and all classifications then follow unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The proofs of {Ξ_{spec_ap,ε}, Ω_X} ∈ Σ_2^G and {Ξ_{spec_ap}, Ω_X} ∈ Π_3^G (restated in thm2's three-limit bullet) rest on a false sandwich; the stated error-controlled containment is not established as written.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We consider a continuous bijection $F:[0,1]\rightarrow[0,1]$ with $F(0)=0$ and $F(1)=1$ such that
$\Lambda$, the evaluation set, will be pointwise evaluations of the function $F$

issues.failure_explanation: The evaluation set is pointwise evaluation on [0,1], and an SPGA may legitimately query at 0 or 1. Since ∪_{j=−N}^{N−1}S_j = [c_{−N}, c_N) excludes the endpoints, for any algorithm that queries an endpoint the event 'Λ_{Γ_{n_1}}(F) ⊂ ∪_j S_j' has probability 0, so the asserted bound P(·) > 1/2 is false and the inductive adversary construction cannot start. Every F in the class fixes 0 and 1, so endpoint queries receive constant answers and are harmless; the proof just never handles them (unlike thm:disc, which explicitly removes its fixed points from Λ).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add one clause: all F ∈ Ω^δ_{[0,1]} fix 0 and 1, so endpoint queries receive the constant answers 0 and 1; either exclude {0,1} from Λ with this justification or enlarge the query-containment events to permit endpoint queries.
issues.overall_effect: The lower-bound proof of thm:interval is incomplete as written, and thm1's Ω_{[0,1]} lower-bound claim, which relies on it, inherits the gap.
issues.title: thm:interval lower-bound proof: endpoint queries make the stated query-containment event impossible
issues.why_classification: A one-clause repair of a missing routine case; the construction, theorem and advertised scope all survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \mathbb{P}\left(\mathrm{dist}(-1,\Gamma_{n_1}(F_{f^{(1)}}))\geq 1\text{ and }\Lambda_{\Gamma_{n_1}}(F_{f^{(1)}})\subset X_1 \text{ and $F$ is sampled only to within error $\delta_1$}\right)>1/2
a finite set $X_1\subset(-\pi,r_1]$ with $r_1\in(-\pi,0)$ such that

issues.failure_explanation: Restricting the evaluation set is not 'without loss of generality' for a lower bound (weakening the algorithm class makes impossibility easier to prove but does not rule out full-Λ algorithms). As written, the events 'Λ_{Γ_{n_k}}(F) ⊂ X_k ⊂ (−π, r_k]' have probability 0 for any algorithm that queries the right half of the torus (x ∈ (0,π)) or the fibers x ∈ {0, ±π}, so the asserted probabilities > 1/2 are false as stated. The argument is salvageable: since every map in the adversarial family has f symmetric with f(0) = π and f(±π) = 0, right-half queries reveal exactly the mirrored left-half information and the special fibers receive constant answers, so those queries are automatically consistent and the events should be restated to allow them (with r_k the maximal left-half query abscissa).

failure_location.quote: By symmetry of $f$ and $f(0)=\pi$, without loss of generality, we may restrict our argument to $\Lambda$ that sample $f$ on the interval $(-\pi,0)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the query-containment events to allow queries that are automatically consistent across the adversarial family (right half by symmetry, fibers x ∈ {0,±π} with fixed f-values), with the symmetry simulation spelled out.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $F(x,y)=(x,y+f(x))$, where $f:[-\pi,\pi]_{\mathrm{per}}\rightarrow [0,\pi]$ is smooth, symmetric ($f(-x)=f(x)$), $f(-\pi)=0$, $f(0)=\pi$ and non-decreasing on $[-\pi,0]$

issues.failure_explanation: No topological conjugacy between F and G exists. Any conjugacy must map F's invariant circles {x = c} onto G's invariant circles {x = c'} with h(c) ≡ ±f(c) (mod 2π); since f is symmetric (f(x) = f(−x)), injectivity of h forces the sign to differ on (0,π) and (−π,0), so the fiber conjugacies are translations on one half and reflections on the other, which have no common continuous limit on the circles {x = 0} and {x = ±π} where the sign flips. Moreover such an h has |h'| = |f'| ≠ 1, so even a mod-0 measurable conjugacy is not measure-preserving and would not give unitary equivalence of the Koopman operators. Part (a) is nevertheless true: on each y-Fourier mode K_F acts as multiplication by e^{inf(x)}, and since the strictly monotone f has finite level sets, the spectral measures are atomless off span{1}.

failure_location.quote: For (a), note that the map $F$ is $C^0$ conjugate to $G(x,y)=(x,y+x)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the conjugacy argument with the direct decomposition: K_F acts on each y-Fourier mode as multiplication by e^{inf(x)}, and strict monotonicity of f makes its level sets finite, so the spectral measures of any g ∈ span{1}^⊥ are continuous; the lemma and all downstream results then stand.
issues.overall_effect: technical_lemma3(a) is unproven as stated; thm:torus (and the main-text thm4) invoke the lemma for both phases of the alternating adversary construction, so their lower-bound proofs are incomplete as written.
issues.title: technical_lemma3(a) proved via a false C^0-conjugacy claim
issues.why_classification: The stated proof is invalidated by a false premise and must be replaced by a contained but genuinely new (standard) argument; the lemma itself is true and no result is lost, so this is not serious.
